subject: Tenant departure — request for proof of destruction & custody evidence
messages:
From: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@biocent.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Customer departure: proof of destruction and chain-of-custody

Hi Naomi —

We’re approaching our end-of-term on the Private / VPC deployment and need to lock down the offboarding checklist from a security/compliance perspective. Specifically, our InfoSec team needs: 

- A clear timeline for full destruction of Biocent tenant data (object store, KV caches, snapshots/backups) once we trigger termination.
- A chain-of-custody record showing the operations performed (who/when) and any automated background jobs that operate on tenant data during deletion.
- Proof that any customer-managed keys can be rotated/destroyed such that data becomes irrecoverable (we use our own KMS customer keys).
- Clarification on whether cloud provider-level snapshots/replicas may retain data outside your control and how you address that.

We will also need a signed attestation/cert of destruction for audit purposes (SOC2 and our internal audits). Can you outline what evidence you can provide and an expected turnaround?

Thanks,
—Amelia Ross
CISO, Biocent Therapeutics
security@biocent.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Ross <amelia.ross@biocent.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Customer departure: proof of destruction and chain-of-custody

Hi Amelia —

Thanks for the clear list. High level up front: yes, we can produce a tenant-scoped evidence package and signed attestation. Below is an overview of what we can provide and the typical timeline; I’ve attached a short process doc and a chain-of-custody template for your auditors.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Tenant-level deletion: supported. Redwood Private maintains logical separation for tenant object stores, KV caches, and snapshot records. When you trigger tenant deletion we run a deterministic sequence that: revokes active tokens, removes tenant logical objects, deletes snapshots, and zeros/overwrites ephemeral caches where supported by underlying runtime.
- KMS / keys: Supported with customer-managed keys (CMK). When customers bring a CMK (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, or HSM-based), Redwood performs encryption operations but does not retain plaintext. We can coordinate a key-rotation + scheduled key-destruction with your KMS admin; destroying the CMK renders ciphertext irrecoverable.
- Cloud snapshots & replicas: We will enumerate snapshot lifecycle and snapshot locations; for hosted cloud disks we either delete snapshots via cloud APIs (with confirmation logs) or hand off instructions for provider-assisted snapshot purge if your tenancy created cross-project copies.
- Evidence we deliver: operation audit log export scoped to tenant, a signed attestation (.pdf), cryptographic key destruction logs (or KMS job history), and our chain-of-custody spreadsheet populated with operation IDs and timestamps.

Planned deliverables and timing (typical):
1) Initial evidence package (audit log slice, deletion runbook excerpt, sample attestation): 3–5 business days after change window is scheduled.
2) Complete chain-of-custody (fully populated, with operation IDs): 5–10 business days (depends on retention window for provider logs).
3) Signed certificate of destruction: 5 business days after final deletion completes.

Notes and caveats:
- If you manage your KMS keys, key destruction is under your control; Redwood will provide KMS job IDs and signed confirmation that data volumes referencing the key were in a deleted state at time of destruction.
- If your deployment has cross-region replication enabled at the cloud level outside Redwood’s control, those replicas must be identified separately. We can assist with discovery and provide steps/contacts.
- For on-prem/private air-gapped installs, physical media destruction (if ever required) will be done with certified vendors; we can include vendor attestation.

Next step: if you’d like we can schedule a 45-minute technical walk-through with Karthik and Olga this week to collect tenancy identifiers and confirm snapshot/replica topology. After that, we’ll produce the sample evidence package.

Attachments: redwood_vpc_deletion_process_v1.pdf, chain_of_custody_template.xlsx

Regards,
Naomi Feldman

On Fri, 11 Jun 2027 at 09:35, Naomi Feldman wrote:
> Hi Amelia —
>
> Thanks for the clear list. High level up front: yes, we can produce a tenant-scoped evidence package and signed attestation.

Thanks Naomi — that helps. A few clarification points before we kick off the walk-through: 

1) Snapshots/backups: do you tag snapshots with tenant IDs so you can prove deletion of only Biocent data (we need tenant-granular proof, not just project-level)?
2) If our CMK is destroyed, can Redwood still demonstrate that no off-site backups exist that would allow recovery (we need assurance that there are no out-of-band copies retained by any provider or 3rd-party process)?
3) What does the attestation include? We need the attester to sign with an org-level role (security or ops lead) and include the procedure ID + related runbook reference.

Also, can you confirm whether deletion operations are synchronous (completed during the change window) or whether background jobs (asynchronous GC) may continue after the window — auditors will ask for timing guarantees.

Appreciate it — if you can confirm these three items we’ll schedule the technical session.

—Amelia
CISO, Biocent Therapeutics

Subject: Re: Customer departure: proof of destruction and chain-of-custody

Amelia —

Good questions. Short answers first, then specifics.

Short answers: 
1) Yes — snapshots and artifacts created by Redwood are tagged with tenant IDs and we can produce a tenant-scoped deletion log.
2) We will perform a discovery sweep and produce a statement of no-known-external-copies; for cloud-provider managed cross-project copies we include provider deletion confirmations and guidance for customer-owned copies. Complete proof for out-of-band copies depends on whether those copies were created by Redwood or by tenant-managed processes; we’ll enumerate each artifact.
3) Attestation: signed by Redwood Head of Infra Security or delegated Ops Lead; includes procedure ID, runbook link, scope (tenant IDs), timestamps, list of delivered artifacts, and the signature block.

Detailed notes: 
- Tagging: Our storage orchestration applies metadata tags to objects and snapshot records at creation. The deletion job filters on tenant tag and writes an audit event per deleted object-set. We can export the audit events for the tenancy window; those exports include object keys, deletion time, operator ID (system or person), and operation UUIDs.

- Snapshot / backup handling: For managed snapshots created by Redwood in the same project/account, we call provider APIs to delete snapshots and capture delete-confirmation events. For backups that have been copied outside the account (rare, but possible via customer-side tooling historically), we will show the discovery report and provide steps for provider-assisted removal; we cannot delete tenant-owned copies that exist in a separate customer-controlled account without their consent.

- Key destruction / irrecoverability: With a customer-managed KMS key, physical irrecoverability is achieved by destroying the key material in your CMK. Redwood will provide the KMS job IDs and key state transitions showing "Disabled -> PendingDeletion -> Deleted" (or provider equivalent). These transitions plus our audit showing that ciphertext references were removed demonstrate practical irrecoverability. For HSM-backed keys we can include HSM vendor logs where available.

- Timing and asynchronous work: The deletion procedure has a primary synchronous phase (revocation, object deletion, snapshot deletion) that completes inside the agreed change window. A subsequent background phase reconciles provider-side eventual-consistency (for example, provider snapshot index updates) — we record both phases in the audit export. In our standard evidence package we clearly label which operations were synchronous and which were reconciliation steps with expected completion windows (usually within 72 hours for provider index reconciliation, subject to provider guarantees).

- Evidence package contents (example):
  • Audit event slice (CSV) scoped to tenant IDs
  • Deletion operation UUIDs with timestamps and operator details
  • KMS job history references and signed job IDs
  • Provider snapshot deletion receipts (where applicable)
  • Signed attestation (sample attached: sample-attestation-signed.pdf)
  • Chain-of-custody spreadsheet (attached)

Next steps:
1) Please share the tenancy IDs and preferred change window (we’ll propose two time slots).
2) We’ll run an initial discovery and provide the sample evidence package within 3 business days of receiving tenancy IDs.
3) After you review, we’ll complete the full populated chain-of-custody and a signed cert of destruction.

If you want Karthik or Olga to walk the team through the provider-level details (snapshot deletion receipts, KMS job history), they’re available for the deep-dive.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
